recipes.name: Sausage and Sauerkraut
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds kielbasa sausage, cut into 1-inch thick slices

steps.text: Place sauerkraut, caraway seeds, brown sugar, and apple into a large saucepan over medium-low heat, and bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, and cook for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.

Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Place bacon and onion into a skillet over medium heat, and cook until bacon is almost crisp and onion is beginning to brown, about 10 minutes. Stir the bacon mixture into the sauerkraut.
Brown kielbasa sausage in remaining bacon grease in the same skillet until sausage begins to brown, 10 to 15 minutes; stir into the sauerkraut mixture.
Spoon the sauerkraut and sausage mixture into the prepared baking dish. Bake in the preheated oven until bubbling, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sausage and Sauerkraut
raw_recipe.description: Sauerkraut and sausage are cooked with bacon, brown sugar, and apple for balanced flavors in this hearty German-inspired dish that will warm you up.

review.reviewBody: Why do people like Dee say they made a recipe but the completely change all the main ingredients? Then they say it's not good. I made it and it's very good. I don't like caraway seed, so I left that out, but that was optional. Serving suggestions by the original poster are exactly right on.
Great dish. I made the recipe as described, but cooked in it in the slow cooker, and added 1/2 cup apple juice so it wouldn't dry out. Will make again.

My rating is based on the actual recipe given. This is a classic, homestyle recipe with great flavors. The only thing I did differently after tasting the original is add a pinch of salt and pepper. Very nice recipe, thanks for sharing it.

This was so good. I made it in the slow cooker. Cooked and crumbled the bacon then just threw it all in with about a half cup of apple juice as another reviewer suggested. Turned out perfect served over mashed potatoes. Will make this one often!

I had issues with the sauerkraut getting slightly burnt on the bottom, I don't get how you put drained food into a pot and expect it to "simmer"? So I added water to prevent further burning. Though next time I may use some wine to do the job. Other than that difficulty, this recipe gets five stars for tasting AMAZING and working perfectly for my high protein needs

Delish! I used the saute mode on my slow cooker and cooked the bacon and onion, then browning the kielbasa. I drained (but did not rinse) the sauerkraut to achieve the "tang" that we enjoy. I then mixed the bacon-onion mixture with the sauerkraut in a large bowl. I then layered the sauerkraut mixture, browned kielbasa, sauerkraut mixture, and the remaining kielbasas. I set the slow cooker on low for 5 hours--the best sauerkraut and kielbasa ever!!

This was wonderful! I followed the recipe exactly but put everything in the crock pot, I did add 1/2 cup apple sauce after a few hours because it seemed a little dry, that made it moist and terrific! I will definately be making this again and often! Thanks for the great recipe.

I made some minor changes in the approach since I was nearly tripling the recipe for a New Year's Day family dinner. Used 6 lbs of Polska Kielbasa, 3 lbs of saurkraut plus 1/2 head of red cabbage, 3 granny smith apples, 2 large sweet onions diced. Didn't have caraway seeds and used fennel seeds instead, just 2 T, plus only 1/2 cup of sugar (for the tripled recipe). I put it all in a large oven-proof covered pot and skipped the stovetop step. Since it had very little liquid, I added 3 x 16 oz cans of Michigan hard cider. I cooked it in the oven at 325 for 2 hrs and then another 1-1/2 hrs at 300. Took it out of the oven and just let it sit on the stove while I finished the potatoes (smashed baby potatoes, very tasty). Even my doubters who were not fond of saurkraut (because it was too acidy) loved it! Not a hint of acid. The final verdict from the 12 family members at the table, from 1-1/2 yrs to 80 years old - YUM!!!! We'll be making it again next year, for certain!!

PERFECT!!!! I made this for our office Pot Luck. We had a Winter Olympics potluck where everyone picked a country and cooked something from that country (cool right? That's what I thought too). My heritage is German, so I picked Germany. This recipe is the closest I've EVER come to the sauerkraut recipe that my grandmother used to make! I followed the recipe BUT used 4 lbs. of sauerkraut, added a smidge more caraway seeds and a little more than 1/4 cup brown sugar. THEN...my roommate came home and suggested I add beer....so I added 1/2 bottle of Blue Moon. O M G...this was not only good...BUT...it was a hit with the coworkers that liked sauerkraut. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!

One more thing...I browned the bacon and onions...cut up the sausage and browned it in the bacon grease and then threw everything in the slow cooker overnight. PERFECTION!!

I've made this several times and it's the best recipe I've found for sausage and sauerkraut. I do add a juice box of apple juice and about 1 or 1-1/2 cups of water to keep it moist. I cook the bacon in 2 large skillets and, after removing it, then I saute the onions and then finally the kielbasa. So delicious!

I have been making this for several years, but I don't bake it. I do everything in a large skillet. I add everything all at once except the kielbasa. Definitely add the caraway seed. When the sauerkraut is almost done, I add the kielbasa until heated through and browned. Thanks for the alternate bake option (for me, anyway). It will cut down stirring to prevent burning and constant watching. Oh, I don't add bacon; in my opinion, it would fight with the flavors of the kielbasa. Seems everyone is adding bacon to everything these days. If anyone is worried about the extra grease, leave this out.

I love this recipe. I had to make a few adjustments. I don't know why you want to rinse the kraut, I love the tangy flavor of full on kraut. I browned 3 polish sausages and sat aside. Sliced up a Granny Smith apple and put it in with a half jar of real deal polish kraut which is less tangy. Added another 1/2 c of good ol homestyle Jarred kraut and simmered for 15 minutes. Sliced up my sausages, put them and 1/4 c of Brown sugar into the mix, covered for 20 minutes. Not sure why we need an hour in the oven. This was delish! Next time I'll follow the recipe as written and see if it is worth the extra effort. I have done sausages and kraut for what seems like a century, never have I added brown sugar, but I will be making this adjustment from now on. Delicious !

I followed the recipe as written except that I chose not to rinse, just drained the sauerkraut since we like the flavor of vinegar. I also saved the brine and was glad I did! I added most of it, almost 3/4 of it back, out of need- the sauerkraut mixture when simmering was very dry and started sticking to the bottom of the pan. Two suggestions to reduce the labor load: 1. Brown the kielbasa whole then slice it into 1" coins. (The kielbasa loses any crunchiness anyways once added to the sauerkraut mixture.) 2. Secondly, same with the bacon. Cook slices whole then cut into pieces. Both suggestions will reduce lots of unnecessary work (browning & turning over 40+ pieces of kielbasa and even more cut up bacon pieces. I assure these suggestions won't change the final tasty outcome. We brought this dish to an Oktoberfest, and it was a HUGE hit!! I had zero leftovers to bring home! I will definitely make this again.
Tasted great! I too used slow cooker. I'll try oven next time.

I love this recipe and have been using it for years……. I am not a caraway fan usually and omitted it for a long time. I finally decided to just go for it and it is a definite win…. But I only use half the amount. I also add just a little water (2TBSP)to the kraut as it cooks and have used apple juice when I have it…., I find it just helps the cook a little .

OK, this recipe takes quite a bit of time, but the prep is pretty easy. So some changes that you'll need to make include the following. First, there needs to be liquid added regularly during the cook. I didn't have any apple juice so I added water (about 1.5 cups) and a splash of apple cider vinegar. Second, I'd recommend cooking the bacon first and then add the onions towards the end of the cook or with the kielbasa. Adding the onions and bacon together caused me to scramble and try to get the onion out before they burned since the bacon wasn't done cooking. Last, one hour on the oven would be too long. I cooked mine 45 minutes and probably should have went closer to 30 minutes. If I cooked this again, I would not rinse the saurkraut either.
Great recipe, did not use caraway because I didn’t have it. Was awesome served over mashed potatoes.!
We make it in the slow cooker- very good

I followed the recipe and it came out so offensively sweet that to eat the remainder I'll have to rinse it under the faucet and drain it. Since no one else has mentioned excess sweetness, I know I did something wrong, but do not know what. It's a simple recipe! I used Bubbies sauerkraut, Eckrich skinless polish kielbasa, and light brown sugar because that' s what I had on hand. Left out bacon to reduce calories. I read that Bubbies has a tangy taste but it doesn't seem like a tangy taste would be cloying. Was so looking forward to making sauerkraut and sausage a regular menu item but it's out of the question until I figure out what went wrong.

Great winter meal. Served over mashed potatoes. Used good Polish sauerkraut so didn't cook it 2 hrs, just warmed it up with the sugar and apple. Used butter to grease the pan. Only had 1 lb of sausage, but 1 1/2 lbs would have been better. Might cut thinner slices next time to make the pound go farther.
